question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, confirm, deny, and timeout?
rationale: The implementation would create a new config surface and security boundary spanning agent runtime, channel approval UX, plugin hooks, and existing tool policies, so automation should not choose the permanent consent model alone.

options.title: Add a core confirmation gate
options.body: Implement a default-compatible tools.confirmation policy that evaluates response text plus proposed tool calls, preserves existing plugin approvals, and records explicit approve/deny/timeout outcomes.

options.title: Keep this plugin-owned
options.body: Do not add core config now and rely on before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies for security plugins that need approval behavior.

options.title: Defer to a broader auth redesign
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until action-level deny, HITL interrupt, and response-level confirmation are designed as one authorization model.

recommendation.title: Add a core confirmation gate
recommendation.body: Implement a default-compatible tools.confirmation policy that evaluates response text plus proposed tool calls, preserves existing plugin approvals, and records explicit approve/deny/timeout outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans product direction and security defaults beyond one implementation file, and recent history connects steipete to adjacent approval/gateway/security routing.
